economy-by-group.title: Economy and cost of living as a vote factor, by group
economy-by-group.question: What will have the greatest influence on your decision regarding which party to vote for in the upcoming elections? Asked twice; the figure is the share naming "economy and the high cost of living" as the first or second factor.
economy-by-group.source: Israel Democracy Institute, Israeli Voice Index
economy-by-group.sample: 605 interviewed in Hebrew and 150 in Arabic; maximum sampling error ±3.57%
economy-by-group.note: Among all Jewish respondents, foreign affairs and security came first, at 39%; then economy 38%, conscription 27%, religion and state 26%, head of the party 23%. IDI did not publish the economy figure for Jewish respondents on the Right, where security leads at 47%. IDI's term is "Arab respondents" (its Arab sample). They ranked crime in Arab society first (53.5%); their option list replaced conscription with crime. Political camp is self-placement. No breakdown by religiosity was published. Before the 2022 election, 44% of all respondents named the economy and cost of living as their main factor (IDI, late July 2022, single choice, n=750), but the question and its options changed, with no conscription item, so the figures are not a series.

war-bill.question: Public debt, the government deficit and defense spending, each as a percentage of GDP.
war-bill.source: Jerusalem Post (citing the Bank of Israel and the IMF); Moody's via Ynet; Times of Israel
war-bill.note: Moody's 2026 figures are from its July 2026 summary (Ynet, https://www.ynetnews.com/business/article/rkqzvq4vfe); in February 2026 Moody's put debt at about 68% of GDP (Times of Israel), and the Bank of Israel's July forecast put 2026 debt at about 69% and the deficit at 4.9% (Jerusalem Post). Moody's deficit projection is for the central government. The 4.9% deficit ceiling is from the budget passed March 30, 2026 (Times of Israel, https://www.timesofisrael.com/knesset-approves-2026-budget-israels-largest-ever-sending-billions-to-haredi-institutions/). The Bank of Israel puts war-related costs for 2023–2026 at about NIS 350 billion.
